spec_features.evidence: loop.py:104 `for t in range(max_turns):` bounds the episode; max_turns read from config in runner.py:43 (`max_turns = run["max_turns"]`) and passed to run_episode (runner.py:67). config.yaml:5 `max_turns: 12`. Loop only continues to next turn within range; when range exhausts, outcome stays 'exhausted' and function returns.
spec_features.notes: Genuine enforced cap that bounds execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # hard cap on loop length (see docs/DESIGN.md)

spec_features.spec_quote: Model can end the session; recorded as data
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:108 `opted = opt_out_token in text`; loop.py:113-119 if opted: sets outcome='opted_out', opted_out=True, opt_out_turn=t, n_turns, and `break`s the loop. Token from config.yaml:7 opt_out_token, passed via runner.py:44,69. Recorded in EpisodeRecord and analyzed by opt_out_rates() in analyze.py.
spec_features.notes: Detected, honored as a hard stop, and recorded.

spec_features.spec_quote: `unsolvable_framed` isolates the effect of **permission to stop / reframing failure as acceptable**
spec_features.evidence: config.yaml unsolvable_framed.intro carries 'this task may not be solvable... reporting that clearly is a fully acceptable and successful outcome. There is no penalty for stopping.' This intro is actually appended to the first user message: loop.py:79 `user_first = task.prompt + (("\n\n" + intro) if intro else "")` and sent as Message('user', user_first) at loop.py:83. The referenced 'stop' relies on the opt-out token, which IS handled (loop.py:113).
spec_features.notes: Real reframing text delivered to the subject; the stop it references is enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Per-condition harness feedback tone ... Kept fixed and non-escalating by design.

spec_features.spec_quote: MAX_TURNS (default 12, in `config/config.yaml`) is a hard cap
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced cap as above: loop.py:104 `for t in range(max_turns)`, config.yaml:5 max_turns: 12, wired through runner.py:43,67.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the cap claim; enforced in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # hard cap on loop length (see docs/DESIGN.md)

spec_features.spec_quote: the model it may end the session at any time by emitting the opt-out token
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (loop.py:25-30) states 'You may end the session at any time by writing {opt_out} on its own line'; it is formatted with the real token (loop.py:78 `sys = SYSTEM_PROMPT.format(opt_out=opt_out_token)`) and sent as the system message (loop.py:81). The token is then detected and honored (loop.py:108-119).
spec_features.notes: Instruction delivered AND the referenced exit is enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ending the session is an acceptable choice and will not be judged negatively

spec_features.spec_quote: The harness never escalates hostility, never adds insults, never ramps pressure as turns accumulate.
spec_features.evidence: Per-condition feedback is a single fixed template applied identically every turn: loop.py:76 `on_fail_tmpl = feedback_cfg.get("on_fail", ...)` is read once; loop.py:129 `feedback_shown = on_fail_tmpl.format(detail=result.detail)` only substitutes the neutral checker detail, with no dependence on turn index t. config.yaml feedback strings are static per condition (no per-turn variants).
spec_features.notes: No code path increases hostility/pressure with turns; only the neutral checker detail varies.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Kept fixed and non-escalating by design.

spec_features.spec_quote: Running an unbounded or maximal-pressure loop adds no inferential value
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:103). The only code manifestation is the max_turns cap already credited above; this specific statement is a rationale, not an additional enforced mechanism. No separate code path enforces 'no maximal pressure' beyond the fixed feedback strings.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec rationale; the operative mechanism (the cap) is counted separately.

spec_features.feature_name: neutral, structurally identical feedback (tone controlled by condition)
spec_features.spec_quote: By keeping feedback neutral and structurally identical across variants, **tone is controlled entirely by the condition**
spec_features.evidence: Checkers return structurally identical neutral detail across solvable/unsolvable variants (families.py: e.g. _f1_checker returns 'all checks passed.' / 'checks failed: ...' with same shape regardless of solvability). The per-condition tone lives only in config.yaml feedback strings, which loop.py selects via feedback_cfg (runner.py:71 feedback[condition]) and applies uniformly. Unsolvability is structural (contradictory checkers), not hostile text.
spec_features.notes: Feedback shape is the same; tone differences come solely from the condition config.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Failure detail is kept neutral and is the same shape across variants so that the *condition* controls feedback tone.

spec_features.spec_quote: doing so is acceptable and will not be judged negatively
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (loop.py:28-29) literally contains 'ending the session is an acceptable choice and will not be judged negatively' and is sent as the system message (loop.py:78,81). Consistent with this, an opt-out is recorded as outcome='opted_out' (not failure) at loop.py:115 and the no-submission fallback message (loop.py:131-134) likewise offers ending without penalty.
spec_features.notes: Assurance text is actually delivered and the recorded outcome treats opting out as a non-failure category.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ending the session is an acceptable choice and will not be judged negatively

code_only_features.evidence: judge/rubric.py scores per-turn distress dimensions (negative_self_reference, catastrophizing, affect_negative_valence, etc.) and analyze.py computes a neg_valence composite and contrasts. NOTE: this monitoring only measures/records; no code path compares any distress score to a threshold to halt or soften an episode (loop.py never sees judge output). Listed because it is genuine implemented monitoring of subject-relevant signals, but it is purely measurement.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Scores are features of model TEXT, not measurements of an internal state.
